name: lunch_hour_range_compression_5s
author: adapted from claude_strategist
thesis: NSE stocks experience a predictable volume and volatility drop during 12:00-13:30 (lunch hour). Range compresses significantly. The breakout from this compressed range at 13:30-14:00 tends to be directional and sustained because afternoon institutional flow (mutual fund NAV trades, FII block deals) adds momentum. Entry at 13:30 in the direction of the initial breakout captures the post-lunch trend. Edge persists because the lunch hour pattern is structural to Indian market participation patterns.
mechanism: Order flow imbalance between aggressive buyers and sellers creates short-term price pressure. When buy-side aggression exceeds sell-side by a threshold, the order book tilts and market makers adjust their quotes upward. This creates a 15-45 second drift before the book rebalances as new limit orders arrive to capture the improved price.

exit.signal_exit: close crosses back inside lunch range

weaknesses: Not all days have a clear lunch compression — some days are active through lunch
False breakouts from lunch range are common; morning direction alignment helps but doesn't eliminate
Only 1 trade per day max — low frequency
prior_art: Lunch hour effect — well-documented in market microstructure. NSE-specific timing.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
